summary: Overall, the notebook is high quality: it runs end-to-end, is reproducible, and uses a proper train/test split with a preprocessing pipeline that avoids data leakage. The key finding is a solid-but-not-perfect model performance (AUC ~0.73) and a clear business signal that customers on monthly contracts—especially those with complaints and late payments—are more likely to churn, though recall at the default threshold is low. In the interview, verify she can clearly explain how the Pipeline/ColumnTransformer prevents leakage, what AUC means in business terms, and how she would choose a decision threshold (and evaluate it) to improve recall without creating too many false alarms. Also ask how she would set up a time-based/temporal validation to ensure the model holds up in production.
